subject: Urgent: BrightWave request latency & 5xx spike in us-west-2 — proposed routing failover
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightwave.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High request latency and 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a rising 5xx rate for calls routed to us-west-2 starting ~07:45 PDT. Median p50 latency has jumped from ~90ms to ~1.2s and 5xx is ~1.8% of requests over the last 25 minutes. This is affecting our checkout flow and causing payment failures for some customers.

We've attached a zip with sample error traces and a short HAR for a failing session (brightwave_error_log_0322.zip). Can Redwood confirm if this is a region/AZ level problem or something specific to our account? We need either an immediate mitigation or a rollback to the last stable model variant.

Our infra lead is cc'd (infra@brightwave.ai). We're happy to approve a cross-region traffic shift if that's the quickest fix but need to understand expected downtime, session stickiness implications, and any data residency concerns.

Ticket: BR-8821

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform, BrightWave


From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Infra <infra@brightwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: High request latency and 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Team — forwarding an urgent production escalation from BrightWave (BW-3919). Symptoms: large latency regression (~1.2s median), 5xx ~1.8%, started ~07:45 PDT. Customer is open to cross-region shift.

Ask: can SRE/ops confirm scope (AZ vs region vs networking) and propose an immediate mitigation path? Options I see:
- controlled traffic shift to us-west-1 (cross-region) with prefix/KV cache warmup;~8–12 minute window
- local AZ evacuation (shift within us-west-2 to healthy AZs) if purely AZ-level
- rollback to previous model variant for BrightWave only (if model-level regression)

Please reply with recommended action, estimated timeline, and any gating items (exec approval, cost implications, data residency). I'm on call and will coordinate with Samira — will need a short one-page runbook or checklist we can execute.

I'll patch updates into HubSpot ticket BR-8821.

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Infra <infra@brightwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: High request latency and 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Quick technical summary from ops: we've seen elevated network retry rates and packet loss concentrated on us-west-2a hosts running the customer-facing inference pool. System telemetry (latency histograms, host error counters) points to an AZ-level networking degradation rather than a model/regression issue.

Recommended immediate plan (minimal blast radius):
1) Controlled traffic diversion: move BrightWave's traffic off us-west-2a to a healthy AZ in the same region (us-west-2b) by updating routing policy for their project. This requires:
   - update routing policy (2–3 steps in console)
   - warm KV/prefix cache for top-10 prefixes (we can pre-warm using replay)
   - monitor token latencies and error rates for 10 minutes
2) If latency/error rates don't improve within 10 minutes, escalate to cross-region diversion to us-west-1 with a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Runbook attached (runbook-cross-region-failover-v2.pdf).

Gating items: customer approval for the cross-AZ move (same region so low risk), and if we go cross-region we need exec sign-off due to potential billing delta and the customer's regulatory note about EU-only data (not applicable to this account but good to confirm). Estimated time to initial diversion to another AZ: 8–12 minutes; cross-region staged rollout: ~25–40 minutes.

I will own the execution with Sean (traffic changes) and Rishi (KV warmup & monitoring).

— Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Infra <infra@brightwave.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High request latency and 5xx spike in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Samira — thanks for the signal and for the traces. Per ops (cc'd) here's our immediate mitigation proposal:

Plan A (start now): divert BrightWave traffic away from the suspected bad AZ to a healthy AZ within us-west-2. Steps:
- change routing policy for BrightWave project to exclude us-west-2a (8–12 minutes)
- warm top prefixes (Marissa/Rishi will run pre-warm)
- monitor for 15 minutes; rollback if errors increase

Plan B (if A fails): staged cross-region shift to us-west-1 (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with a 30–40 minute window and continuous monitoring.

Risks: small window of duplicate requests for some sessions during cache warmup; possible short-lived increases in 429s while autoscaling stabilizes.

Please reply with one of the following so we can act:
- APPROVE (do AZ diversion now)
- DECLINE (don't touch routing)
- ASK Q (I'll call to discuss)

I'll execute on APPROVE and update HubSpot BR-8821 and the status page: https://status.redwood.example.com/incidents/2027-03-22-usw2-network-flap

— Priyom

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: cto@redwood.com, ceo@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Exec alignment: BrightWave incident & routing decision

Thanks for the quick triage. I approve the controlled AZ diversion as described. Please proceed with Plan A immediately if BrightWave approves. Marissa/Sean/Rishi — document any anomalies and capture the timeline so we can include it in a post-incident brief.

I also want an executive 15-minute incident brief at 15:00 PST with a one-slide summary: impact, fix performed, customer impact, and follow-up actions. Prio on root-cause determination and whether any changes to our smart-routing fallback rules are needed to reduce future AZ blast radius.

Prio: get BrightWave stable -> then schedule remediation retrospective.

— Laura
VP Sales (covering Key Accounts)
Redwood Inference
